one_sentence: All substantive fields (author, title, year, volume, number, pages, ISSN) correctly match Pascal Paul (2020), "The Time-Varying Effect of Monetary Policy on Asset Prices," The Review of Economics and Statistics 102(4):690-704 -- no field mixing -- but the entry is a raw Web of Science export with stray non-BibTeX fields, an ALL-CAPS journal name, a missing DOI, and a citation key drawn from the author's given name rather than surname.

issues.corrected: The Review of Economics and Statistics
issues.reason: ALL-CAPS is Web of Science's internal rendering, not the journal's actual name. Confirmed against CrossRef and the MIT Press journal landing page: the published title is 'The Review of Economics and Statistics.'

No DOI field was present despite this being a published MIT Press journal article with a registered DOI. Confirmed via CrossRef lookup on the DOI, which returns matching title/author/journal/volume/issue/pages/ISSN/EISSN.

Not a standard BibTeX field; this is a Web of Science export artifact. Harmless to a .bst style that ignores unknown fields, but should be stripped for a clean bibliography -- ORCID belongs in author metadata, not the reference list.
A Web of Science accession number, not a BibTeX field recognized by any standard style. Pure WoS export residue.

Non-standard BibTeX field (another WoS export artifact); standard styles use ISSN only. Value itself is correct (confirmed via CrossRef as the journal's electronic ISSN) but the field has no consumer in typical .bst/biblatex styles and clutters the entry alongside ORCID-Numbers/Unique-ID.

The BibTeX key is the author's GIVEN name ('Pascal'), not the surname ('Paul'), which is the opposite of standard convention (typically 'paul2020' or 'paul2020timevarying'). This is a smell worth flagging since it suggests the entry was auto-generated from a WoS record without normalization, but it is not changed here because renaming the key would break every \cite{pascal} reference elsewhere in the paper; a rename should be a coordinated find-and-replace, not a silent fix in this report.

Minor cosmetic: WoS three-letter abbreviation normalized to a full month name/standard BibTeX month macro convention. Not a factual error (the article's cover-date month is October 2020, per MIT Press).
